title: The Office party nobody wanted
dek: Mandatory fun, a lukewarm sheet cake and someone has brought a guitar. Twelve questions to reveal which Dunder Mifflin employee you are when the boss is watching.

questions.prompt: 4:58pm on a Friday. The printer jams with something confidential still in it.

options.label: Pull the page, say nothing
Read enough to be useful later
Announce the printer is haunted
Fix it properly, then go

questions.prompt: Your calendar has a meeting called 'sync'. No agenda, no end time, six people.

options.label: Accept, then ask for the agenda
Decline with 'let's take this async'
You're already in it. You never left
Bring snacks. It's a party now
The desk nobody walks behind
No meetings after four

questions.prompt: I'd rather be trusted than promoted.
I've written 'per my last email' and meant it.
A laminated sign on the microwave reads DO NOT REHEAT FISH. It has been ignored for a year.

options.label: Add a second sign, laminated
Reheat fish. Make eye contact
Take the sign down. Live free
Start a list of who ignores it

questions.prompt: If the work is done, the hours are nobody's business.
Pick the plant for your desk.

options.label: Cactus, one spine missing
options.alt: A small cactus in a pot on a desk

options.label: Fern, far too big for the desk
options.alt: A large leafy fern in a pot

options.label: Monstera, blocking half the screen
options.alt: A monstera plant with broad leaves

options.label: Four succulents in a neat row
options.alt: A row of small succulents in pots

questions.prompt: The office chat is buzzing and you've been tagged in a thread from 2019.

options.label: Reply as if it was yesterday
Read all of it, say nothing
Mute it. It's a work chat
Bring it up at lunch

questions.prompt: I have a work personality that comes off like a costume.
questions.high: I take it off in the car

questions.prompt: A work party is still work.
The boss asks for a fun fact. In the meeting. Everyone.

options.label: Say something mildly alarming
Give a fact about the company
Make one up on the spot
Turn it into a bit that runs long

results.name: Michael Scott
results.tagline: Hostage to an audience of any size
results.blurb: You believe, genuinely, that work is about people. You'll remember a birthday, organise the awful party and give a toast that goes on too long — and half of it will land. Your instincts are warm, your timing is a coin flip, and the place would be a lot colder without you.
strengths: Makes a room feel like it belongs to everyone
Cares about people beyond their output
Commits to the bit, every time
results.watchOut: The joke is not always the moment. Read the room before you take the microphone.

results.name: Dwight Schrute
results.tagline: Prepared for a crisis that hasn't happened
results.blurb: You are the only person who read the whole policy, and you'd like that noted. You respect the ladder, the process and the correct way to label a folder. People laugh at the thoroughness right up until the day it saves them.
results.watchOut: Rules aren't the point; people are. Break one, on purpose, for someone.

results.name: Jim Halpert
results.blurb: You're the person who sees the absurdity and says nothing — until the perfectly timed glance. You do the job well enough to be left alone, and you save your real energy for the few things and people you actually care about.
strengths: Reads the room without being read
results.watchOut: Detachment is comfortable, but it looks like not caring. Say the sincere thing out loud.

results.name: Pam Beesly
results.blurb: You keep the place running and you're the last to mention it. You notice who's struggling, you soften the email, you make the room less sharp. Under the quiet there's real ambition — you're just waiting until it's safe, or until it isn't.
strengths: Makes difficult people easier to be around
Steady in a crisis nobody labels a crisis
results.watchOut: Waiting to be ready is a way of not starting. Put one honest thing on the table.

results.name: Kelly Kapoor
results.blurb: You are the social engine: the gossip, the calendar, the reason anyone knows anything. You feel things at full volume and you don't pretend otherwise. Underneath the drama is a genuinely sharp read on people and a fierce need to be included.
strengths: Makes work feel less like work
results.watchOut: Not every silence is about you. Let one thing go by without a verdict.

results.name: Creed Bratton
results.blurb: You are unbothered in a way other people find suspicious. You do just enough, disappear at the right moment, and have a whole life nobody at work will ever hear about. It's not laziness — it's a very healthy boundary, badly explained.
results.watchOut: Vanishing all the time means nobody knows what you're good at. Show up once, fully.

results.name: Angela Martin
results.blurb: You have a correct way of doing things and a quiet despair that nobody follows it. You keep the party on schedule, the cake cut properly and the nonsense to a minimum. Your disapproval is famous; your loyalty is the part people miss.
strengths: Protective of the people who earn it
results.watchOut: Right and warm can coexist. Try one kind sentence before the correction.

results.name: Ryan Howard
results.blurb: You're here but you're also somewhere else — mentally building the thing you'd rather be doing. You're smart, easily bored, allergic to being managed, and you'll reinvent yourself the second the room gets stale.
results.watchOut: The next thing won't fix the boring part. Finish one thing properly here first.
